questions: When did you first notice the difference in your pupil size?
Have you experienced any double vision?
Have you had any pain in or around your eye?
Have you noticed any drooping of your left eyelid?
Are you able to look down and read something, or look up at something on a high shelf without difficulty?
Have you noticed if the pupil difference becomes less noticeable when you focus on something close to you?
Did the pupil size difference and eye movement difficulty start suddenly or gradually over time?
Have you experienced any headaches, especially in the back of your head or around the eyes?
Have you had any tremors, stiffness, or problems with balance and walking?
Have you ever been treated for syphilis in the past?
Do you have any history of trauma to the head or eyes?
orders: Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) of the intracranial vessels, focusing on the circle of Willis and posterior communicating arteries, to evaluate for aneurysm.
Formal pupillometry assessment - measure pupil diameters in ambient light, test for relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD), and document the near response in detail.
Assessment of ptosis - measure palpebral fissure heights in primary gaze and assess for any subtle eyelid retraction or weakness.

MRI brain with dedicated thin-cut sequences through the midbrain (axial and sagittal T2-weighted, FLAIR, and diffusion-weighted imaging) to evaluate for structural lesion or infarction in the mesencephalic tegmentum.
Blood tests: complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level, and antinuclear antibody (ANA).

Detailed examination of the tonic pupil - specifically assess for tonic near response (sustained constriction during accommodation) and look for vermiform/segmental pupillary oscillations under slit lamp examination.
served: lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides)
